conviction_note: No company-level unpriced number turned up; the filed items are proxies that roughly offset. Input costs (HRC steel +8% and diesel +20% since the 17 July guide assumptions) lean negative, and AZZ's 13 October coatings print plus VMI's run of EPS beats lean positive. So impact_sum is -0.2, and the scaled number is p_up 48 on an abs_move_pct of 7.0, which is -0.28. The two measures agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $5.71-5.72, revenue $1.11-1.12B (Earnings Whispers https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/vmi, whisper $5.81; aggregator search agreeing at $5.72 / $1.11B). Company FY2026 guide (21 July 2026): EPS $22.25-23.50, sales $4.30-4.45B, Infrastructure $3.4-3.5B, Agriculture $0.90-0.95B unchanged (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000102729/000110465926085223/vmi-20260721xex99d1.htm). H1 EPS was $11.65, so the guide implies H2 $10.60-11.85. Q3 consensus of $5.72 sits mid-range, which puts it inside the guide. Sales guide implies H2 $2.15-2.30B, about $1.075-1.15B a quarter, so the revenue bar also sits inside the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 417,622 shares at the 30 Sep 2026 settlement, down from 455,191; about 2.2% of shares outstanding; days to cover 1.98 (https://equibles.com/stocks/vmi/shortinterest, read 2026-10-19). Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Skew_25d is +3.59 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI is 1.96, but total OI is only 77 and the ATM spread is 28% of mid, so the chain is thin and the skew is a weak statement. The stock is -22.8% from its 52-week high (585.71), -4.0% over 20 days and -3.6% over 5 days, with no company filing or news since July to explain it. Unusual Whales on 6 Oct priced the earnings move at +/-8.44%.

findings.finding: US hot-rolled coil has kept rising after the 17 July date to which Valmont pinned its steel assumption ('steel costs aligned with futures prices as of July 17, 2026'). Nucor CSP was $1,135/st on 20 July and $1,230 on 5 October (+8%); spot is about $1,210-1,220 against $825-865 a year earlier (+40% YoY). On the Q2 call the CFO said steel was already up 27-30% YTD, that material inflation 'accelerated' in Q2 and would hit Q3, and that price pass-through comes with a lag. Infrastructure margin was guided flat to H1 (17.6% in Q2). The risk lands mainly on the Q4 implied in the FY guide and on margin commentary, not on Q3 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (21 Jul): beat ($6.14 vs $5.80) and raise, yet the stock fell -3.9% on a call that flagged accelerating material inflation. Q1 2026 +11.9% on a beat with margin expansion.
findings.why_not_priced: Steel prices are public, but consensus Q3 EPS ($5.72) sits mid-guide, so sell-side has not cut for the further rise. If it were priced, consensus would sit at the guide's low end, not the whisper $0.09 above consensus. The -4% 20-day drift and the downside skew may hold part of it.
findings.independence: Same direction from https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-has-raised-the-price-of-hot-rolled-coils-to-1-230-per-tonne/ (5 Oct letter, $1,230) and Nucor's 17 Sep Q3 guide citing higher average selling prices (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm). All of this is industry proxy; Valmont itself said 'net net' pass-through (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-valmont-industries-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: US on-highway diesel set a record during VMI's fiscal Q3, which ends late September. EIA weekly: $5.31 at end-July, $5.599 on 31 Aug, $5.967 on 7 Sep, then above $6 and $6.38 on 28 Sep, against $3.75 a year earlier. On the Q2 call management had already cited diesel +45% YTD as a cost. The rise feeds outbound freight on heavy utility structures and farmers' operating costs, where USDA puts fuel expense at +28.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The cost line was the stated reason the Q2 beat-and-raise sold off -3.9%. Q3 2025 also beat ($4.98 vs $4.64) and rose only +1.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro series and does not show in the consensus, which is unchanged mid-guide. If it were priced, Q3 EPS estimates would have come down from the post-Q2 level.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Same direction from https://startbusinessbystate.com/?p=16465 (EIA weekly series to 28 Sep, $6.38 vs $3.75 YoY). Shares the input-cost theme with the steel finding but is a different series; merge them if you judge both one concern.

findings.finding: AZZ, the largest US hot-dip galvanizer and a direct peer of VMI's North America Coatings line (+16.6% in Q2), reported on 13 Oct for the quarter to 31 Aug. Metal Coatings sales rose +22.9%, with higher volumes in construction, infrastructure and transportation plus price pass-through, at a 30.7% EBITDA margin. AZZ raised its FY guide to $1.825-1.875B sales. This is the latest counterparty read on US infrastructure steel demand since VMI last spoke on 21 July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Infrastructure strength drove the +11.9% after Q1 2026 and the +17.5% after the Feb 2025 print. Coatings on its own has not been the line the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out 6 days before the print, and VMI fell -3.6% over the 5 sessions that followed. If the market had read it across, the 5-day tape would not be negative. Coatings is a small slice of VMI, though, and the zinc-cost caveat raised in AZZ commentary limits the margin read.
findings.independence: Peer document. Utility demand context from VMI's own Q2 call ('capacity constraints more than demand') at https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-valmont-industries-inc-stock/. A third-party read (https://finsee.ai/earnings/azz/2027/q2/en/) notes AZZ raised sales more than EBITDA, which implies cost pressure and cuts against the margin half of this finding.

findings.finding: VMI has a consistent EPS beat pattern into this print: Q3 2025 $4.98 vs $4.64 consensus (+7%), Q2 2026 $6.14 vs $5.80 (+6%), and Q1 2026 also beat with EPS +27.5% YoY. The Q3 2026 bar of $5.72 is +15% YoY, below Q2's $6.14, and sits mid-guide. Earnings Whispers' whisper of $5.81 is already above it. With $451M of buyback authorization left after $60M in Q2, share count keeps falling. A beat of about 2-5% is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are not reliably bought here. Q2 2026 beat and raised and the stock fell -3.9%; Q3 2025 beat and rose +1.36% after trading down intraday; Q4 2025 (Feb 2026) fell -6.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the whisper above consensus shows the street expects a beat. What is not priced is the size of the beat against a consensus that has stayed mid-guide despite the cost inflation.

findings.finding: Agriculture demand stays soft into the seasonally weak H2. USDA's 3 Sep forecast cut 2026 net farm income to $158.4B (-2.6% YoY) with record production expenses of $492.8B (+4.5%, fuel +28.8%). Lindsay's last print (quarter to May) had North America irrigation -11% and Brazil volumes lower. VMI kept its ag guide at $0.90-0.95B, which implies H2 ag of $431-481M against $469M in H1, and guided H2 ag margins to the 'low teens' and 'minimal' Middle East projects. Net of the rest of the company: ag is about 20% of sales, while Infrastructure (about 80%) is guided +; for this to matter, ag would have to land below the guide floor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 ag fell -9% with an $11M Brazil bad debt, and the stock still rose +1.36%. Ag weakness has been looked through while Utility grows.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company already guided ag down 6-11% and low-teens H2 margins. What is new since July is the higher fuel and fertilizer cost estimate, which weighs on grower capex decisions for the fall season.
findings.independence: Lindsay FQ3 release, a direct irrigation peer: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000836157/000119312526293405/lnn-ex99_1.htm. It also says the MENA project is on schedule despite geopolitics, which cuts slightly against a further Middle East hit.

findings.finding: The 10-Q filed 28 July discloses a 1 June 2026 proclamation that cut the US-melted steel threshold for the 10% Section 232 rate on utility poles from 95% to 85%. VMI imported about $220M of fabricated structures from Mexico in FY2025 and expects most Mexico-made poles to qualify for the 10% rate, which limits the tariff cost on Utility.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on tariffs explicitly. The guide's low end was described as covering tariff-regulation changes.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the guide includes tariffs in effect on 17 July, so this sits inside the guide. The residual is lower risk at the guide's low end, which could support a narrowing upward.

baseline_tension: The small net-negative lean agrees with the downside skew (+3.59, though on a 77-contract chain) and the -4% 20-day drift, so it is probably partly priced. The positive peer read (AZZ) and the beat pattern cut against the drift. Net: close to a coin flip.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): VMI sold its Q2 beat-and-raise (-3.9%), so the beat-pattern finding goes from +0.4 to +0.2.

Rule 7 (positioning): the negatives on steel and diesel agree with the downside skew and are probably partly priced. They shrink from -0.6 to -0.5 and from -0.4 to -0.3. Short interest was checked (2.2%, DTC 2.0, not crowded).
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): ag is about 20% of sales against a guided-up Infrastructure, so the ag finding goes from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Section 232 threshold change is already in the 17 July guide assumptions, so it goes from +0.2 to +0.1.
Left standing: the AZZ peer print (+0.5), a counterparty document published after VMI last spoke. abs_move_pct 7.0 and p_up 48 are unchanged; the net sum is unchanged at -0.2.
